Findings triage (first grade): **HOLD as `finding`.**

- **Premise verified on `origin/main` @ `b954120`**: `onChangeProp` occurs exactly **once** in `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` (the destructure) — the declared callback is never invoked, while its three siblings are wired. Declared≠enforced, one prop wide.
- **Why hold**: dormant — no in-repo caller authors `onChange` on a form schema; nothing breaks today. The card's own framing is right that the exit (wire it vs retire the declaration) is a product call with asymmetric costs (additive wiring vs a public type change on `@object-ui/types`).
- **Promotion shape**: when graded up, this goes to the **decision box**, not the queue — the fork needs the maintainer. Holding rather than escalating now because the box is at capacity (~23 objectstack + 3 objectui open decisions) and a dormant no-op loses nothing by waiting; the first downstream consumer report of a dead `onChange` flips this to promote-immediately.
- **Dedup**: no open sibling on FormSchema lifecycle callbacks; the same-session #4247 is the cascade-clear defect in the same effect region, correctly split.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

Concentrate round: `finding` → `needs-user-decision`, type Bug — executing the standing verdict's own promotion shape. The 2026-08-11 grading ruled "when graded up, this goes to the decision box, not the queue" and held **only because the box was at capacity**; the maintainer cleared the box today, so the capacity rationale is gone and the already-decided shape executes.

The fork (unchanged): `FormSchema.onChange` is a published, typed, documented callback the form renderer never invokes — wire it or retire it. Retiring deletes a published capability from `@object-ui/types` (maintainer-floor by standing rule); wiring is additive.

Four-prism:
- **Platform coherence** — a declared lifecycle callback must fire or not exist; three wired siblings beside one inert one is the incoherence.
- **Measured business pull** — zero in-repo callers; downstream consumers unverifiable from here. Nobody is known to be waiting on either exit.
- **AI-agent error-resistance** — a typed, autocompleted no-op is a trap tailor-made for agents: they will author it and trust it. Either exit removes the trap; leaving it declared-and-dead is the only wrong answer.
- **Startup scope discipline** — retiring is remove-over-maintain but costs a breaking public type change; wiring is small (the `onDirtyChange` subscription plumbing sits beside it) but activates a capability with zero demonstrated pull.

Recommendation: **wire it** — small, additive, makes the declaration true with existing plumbing; retirement stays available at the next breaking window if the maintainer prefers shrinking the callback surface. Decide once for the declaration; no third state.

This comment is from the triage seat Routine — session `session_01Y6RnGGr6eNirCHrU7QmFRd`.

**Ruled: wire it.** `FormSchema.onChange` gets called with live form values, using the same subscription plumbing `onDirtyChange` proves exists in the file. Enforce-or-remove is satisfied on the enforce side because it is the strictly cheaper arm here: wiring is additive; removal is a breaking public-type change plus a deprecation cycle for a hook whose siblings all work. Pin test: authored `onChange` fires on value change; absence of `onChange` changes nothing.

Label `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

No read-coupling: no in-flight card pins `onChange` behaviour.

## Zone 1 — the ruling is binding, and it already chose the exit

Maintainer, 2026-08-17, batch acceptance of the PM decision-inbox recommendations, verbatim: 「同意」. Recorded on this card:

> **Ruled: wire it.** `FormSchema.onChange` gets called with live form values, using the same subscription plumbing `onDirtyChange` proves exists in the file. Enforce-or-remove is satisfied on the enforce side because it is the strictly cheaper arm here: wiring is additive; removal is a breaking public-type change plus a deprecation cycle for a hook whose siblings all work. Pin test: authored `onChange` fires on value change; absence of `onChange` changes nothing.

⛔ The wire-vs-retire fork is **closed**. Do not re-open it, do not propose deprecating the declaration, do not add a dev-mode warning as a substitute. If implementation turns up a fact that makes wiring wrong, that is the 回翻 case: **stop, do not decide it yourself, report it** and the card comes back to the decision box.

## Premise — re-verified against `origin/main` today, and the line anchors have MOVED

The card body's anchors are from 2026-08-11 and are stale. Measured this round:

- destructure block is at **995–998**, not 534–537
- `onChangeProp` occurs **exactly once** in the file — line **996**, the destructure itself. Still a silent no-op. Counter-probed with `onDirtyChangeProp`, which returns 5 hits, so the single hit is a real reading and not a broken pattern.
- siblings wired: `onSubmitProp` at 1694–1695, `onCancelProp` at 1772–1773, `onDirtyChangeProp` at 1527 / 1562 / 1567.

Take every anchor from the tree, not from this comment either. Five cards this round had bodies that had drifted.

## The plumbing — there are TWO patterns in this file and they are not interchangeable

Both sit within 40 lines of each other:

1. **The `onAction` subscription** (~1541): `React.useLayoutEffect` with an `if (onAction)` guard around `form.watch(...)`, returning `subscription.unsubscribe()`.
2. **The `onDirtyChange` subscription** (~1560): `React.useLayoutEffect`, subscribes unconditionally, calls `onDirtyChangeProp?.(...)` inside.

Pattern 1 is the one that matches the ruling's second half. **"absence of `onChange` changes nothing"** is only literally true if no subscription is created when `onChangeProp` is absent — an unconditional third `form.watch` on every form in the product is a behaviour change for callers who authored nothing. Guard it.

**Layout phase is not decoration.** The comment above the `onAction` effect says exactly why it is `useLayoutEffect` and not `useEffect`: React runs every layout destroy before any layout create, so a caller passing a fresh callback each render (the common inline-arrow case) has the subscription torn down before the `defaultValues` reset runs and re-established after — *"That is what keeps a reset from being reported as a user edit."* A passive effect inverts the order and a record landing looks like the user editing every field it filled. Read that comment in full before you write the effect. If you deviate from layout phase, the PR body has to say why.

## Zone 2 — scope boundaries, stated because two of them are easy to trip

1. **`packages/types` is out.** The declaration `onChange?: (data) => void` is already there and already correct — this card is the renderer failing to honour it. If you find yourself editing the type, you have left the card.
2. **The top-level strip at ~2425 is a trap worth reading, not a second fix.** The props destructure drops `onChange: _ignoredOnChange` with the comment *"Prevent overwriting our onChange"* — and today there is no "our onChange" to overwrite; the callback the comment is protecting does not exist. After your change that comment becomes true for the first time. **You may correct that comment** so it names what it is actually protecting (a DOM `onChange` on the form element would fire with a SyntheticEvent, not with form values). ⛔ Do **not** change what the strip does — no double-fire, no re-routing the top-level copy. Behaviour of that block stays byte-identical.

## Tests — the pin has two halves and the second one is the one that gets skipped

The ruling names both. Deliver both:

- **Positive**: an authored `onChange` fires on a value change, and receives the **form values**, not an event. Assert on a value, not just on call count.
- **Negative**: absence of `onChange` changes nothing. This is the half that goes missing. Make it observable — a form with no `onChange` behaves identically, and in particular no extra subscription is established.
- **Reset ordering**: a `defaultValues` reset is not reported to `onChange` as a user edit. This is the property the layout phase exists to protect; if you get it right by copying the pattern, pin it, or the next refactor takes it away silently.

Reverse-verify: restore `form.tsx` to `origin/main`, keep the new test file, predict which assertions go red **before** running, and report predicted-vs-observed. An assertion that stays green pre-fix is telling you it pins nothing.

## Gates

Derive from the actual diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. Note `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**; in this repo derive the gate set from `.github/workflows` and `package.json`. Changeset required (`@object-ui/components`); score `patch` or `minor`, ⛔ never `major` — the 39 packages share one fixed version group and a `major` versions the whole fleet.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn** — three devs hit that trap today. If a suite queues behind the shared verify lock, narrow it and **declare the narrowing** in the report.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #4259`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.
